headline: Growth accelerates and guidance rises, but margins compress
summary_short: DigitalOcean's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 28.6% y/y to $281.2 million, but GAAP operating income fell 17.5% y/y to $29.4 million as stock-based compensation and amortization outpaced the topline gain.
summary_long: Revenue grew 28.6% y/y to $281.2 million, accelerating on record incremental ARR of $93 million and outsized growth among $500K+ and $1M+ customers (+160% and +214% revenue growth, respectively). Gross margin fell 4.9 points y/y to 55.0% and GAAP operating income declined 17.5% to $29.4 million, pressured by higher stock-based compensation ($32.7M vs $21.1M) and amortization; adjusted EBITDA still rose 26.9% to $113.6 million. Cash grew to $767.0 million after an $887.9 million equity raise used partly to retire convertible notes and repay term debt. DigitalOcean raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to approximately 30% growth and initiated Q3 guidance of $304-307 million.

drivers.explanation: CEO cited accelerating growth from highest-spending customers and AI-native workloads landing nine-figure annual commitments, citing early Inference Engine customers driving token consumption up ~30x in 60 days.
Growth attributed to record incremental ARR and outsized gains among $500K+ and $1M+ customers, plus the first nine-figure annual customer commitments signed this quarter.
Cost of revenue grew 44.2% y/y versus 28.6% revenue growth, compressing gross margin 4.9 points; the release does not break out the cost-of-revenue drivers.
Stock-based compensation rose to $32.7M from $21.1M y/y; excluding it (and amortization/impairment), adjusted operating income actually rose 9.3%, per the release's own reconciliation.
Growth reflects revenue scaling faster than adjusted opex once stock-based compensation, acquired-intangible amortization, and a small impairment charge are excluded per the release's reconciliation.
Growth of 26.9% roughly tracked revenue growth, holding adjusted EBITDA margin near-flat at 40% versus 41% a year ago.
Net income fell only 4.3% despite a 36% drop in pretax income, cushioned by an $8.3M income tax benefit this quarter versus a $5.4M tax expense a year ago.
EPS fell faster than net income because weighted diluted shares rose 25.8% y/y to 126.5 million, reflecting dilution from the quarter's follow-on equity offering.
Fell as non-GAAP net income dipped modestly while non-GAAP diluted shares rose to 123.3 million from 100.6 million, again reflecting the equity raise.
Driven by $887.9 million net proceeds from a follow-on public offering, used to fund the repurchase of approximately $472 million of convertible notes and adjust term-loan borrowings.
Increase reflects shares issued in the quarter's follow-on public offering, which funded the convertible-note repurchase described in Recent Developments.
Swing to a $930.7 million balance from a $175.2 million deficit a year ago was driven mainly by additional paid-in capital rising to $925.0 million from the follow-on equity offering.
